A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REDI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and hyperparameter ablations, generation statistics, and qualitative and token-level analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations across model architectures and scales, scientific question answering, and code generation.

M1.justification: Both versions use positive-trace SFT followed by the same asymmetrically weighted, length-normalized positive/negative log-likelihood objective (Equation 5). Calling this objective REINFORCE-style and evaluating additional base models do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds GPQA scientific question answering and HumanEval code generation, substantially extending task coverage. The OpenR1 training data and previous benchmark coverage, including the AIME25 diagnostic example in Appendix F, remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same SFT, DPO, SimPO, symmetric REDI, and external Qwen/DeepSeek comparators. The added generalization experiments compare REDI with SFT; they introduce no new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 extends the experimental configurations beyond Qwen-1.5B to Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B, using SFT followed by one REDI epoch. It also introduces HumanEval continuation-prompt evaluation and pass@5 reporting. Settings for the retained experiments in Appendix C are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix D.2 add explicit tests of generalization across architectures and scales and transfer from mathematical training to science and coding. Existing learning-rate/alpha ablations, case studies, and token analyses remain. The pass@16 analysis is relocated to Appendix D.3, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix C.5 retains the same SEM calculation from benchmark scores indexed by generated sample, and retained tables preserve their uncertainty reporting. No new seeds, independent training repetitions, or statistical tests are documented. New Tables 4–5 provide point estimates only.

E6.justification: Existing main and pass@16 table values remain unchanged. New Table 4 reports SFT/REDI averages of 28.0/32.9 for Llama-3.2-3B and 62.5/65.1 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B. Table 5 adds GPQA scores of 28.3%/35.9% and HumanEval pass@1 scores of 7.1%/19.9%. These are newly reported comparisons, not revisions to earlier scores.

T1.justification: Proposition B.3's proof replaces the bare gradient factor with its norm in the final scalar bound, correcting the mathematical expression. The proposition, small-beta argument, and Appendix A convergence theorem otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion withdraw the state-of-the-art claim for openly trained 1.5B models and emphasize data efficiency and performance comparable to proprietary-data distillation. The contribution statement adds a first-systematic-study claim and reframes REDI as a REINFORCE-style objective rather than emphasizing a novel reference-free loss.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 interprets the new results as evidence of broader applicability and reduced overfitting to mathematical training data. New Section 7 explicitly identifies reliance on a single teacher as a limitation. Existing stability, self-correction, token-dynamics, and future-online-RL interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 specifies LightEval for GPQA and lm-evaluation-harness with continuation prompts for HumanEval. New Appendix G documents asset licenses, provenance, and reuse restrictions. The existing hyperparameters, hardware, timing information, and code URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects REDI to Williams's REINFORCE and substantially revises Section 5 to distinguish it from teacher-guided online RL methods LUFFY, TAPO, and CHORD and concurrent negative-reinforcement research. The earlier IPO discussion and citation are removed, changing positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten, with framework terminology changed to recipe. The detailed pass@16 discussion moves to Appendix D.3, while a limitations section and appendices on licensing, AI assistance, and potential harms are added.

P2.justification: The manuscript changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Two generalization tables are added. The former main-text pass@16 Tables 3–4 become appendix Tables 6–7; the existing training-time table is also relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens external validity: Tables 4–5 address v1's reliance on one student model and predominantly mathematical evaluations through additional architectures, scales, and tasks. More restrained performance claims and clearer research positioning also improve the paper. The new tables lack uncertainty estimates, and Appendix D.2 ambiguously calls its model final Qwen-REDI-1.5B while Table 5's OlympiadBench score matches the three-epoch-initialized variant. These reporting weaknesses temper the transfer conclusions but do not outweigh the broader validation.
